title: Benedetto Fantini (DECODE 'Jantini'), Buda and Eger, to the Este court, 1517-1518 (ASMo, Ambasciatori, Ungheria b. 4, Fantini nos. 5-6; DECODE R1126, R1127; catalogue 156)

documents.shelfmark: ASMo, Ambasciatori, Ungheria b. 4, Benedetto Fantini no. 5 (DECODE R1126; Vestigia 1849)

transcription.source: DECODE images R1126 P1-P6; column transcription of p. 1 only (18 cipher lines); p. 2 (about 26 lines) not transcribed
transcription.notes: Upper/base notation per column. One reader; 137 distinct labels in 581 columns shows the labels are not yet consistent.

documents.shelfmark: ASMo, Ambasciatori, Ungheria b. 4, Benedetto Fantini no. 6 (DECODE R1127; Vestigia 1851)

system.summary: Two-tier signs (a base stroke 7, m, n, g, y, L-bracket with a small sign above or inside), resembling Caprile's 1519 cipher but with a different sign inventory; the unit (letter, syllable or word) is not established.

diacritics.note: The small sign above each base stroke is part of the sign; how it combines with the base is not established.

system.sibling_key: Caprile 1519 two-tier cipher (caprile1519, itself unbuilt) compared: sign inventory differs

prior_solution.where: No decipherment or clear copy in the Vestigia file (Fantini nos. 1-7); none found in print

conditions.human_role: Selected the target; the DECODE session cookie was supplied earlier.

solution.what: Fetched DECODE R1126/R1127 metadata and images; Vestigia search found Fantini's whole file (V1846-V1852), all images fetched.
Sender identified as Benedetto Fantini (DECODE misreads 'Jantini'), Ferrarese agent in Ippolito d'Este's household; only nos. 5 and 6 contain cipher, and no decipherment is in the file.
Column transcription (upper sign / base stroke) of R1126 p. 1, 18 cipher lines, 581 columns.
Homophonic anneal (it-cinquecento 4-grams, unigram penalty) over p. 1 columns, with the frequent 7g/7y signs kept, merged, or treated as nulls: 6 restarts x 60k moves each.

Statistics: the three-column run 7 / g / m-with-b recurs 14 times and 7g or 7y occurs 45 times in 581 columns, too often for one letter per column; 7g and 7y behave like word signs. The unit of the cipher is unresolved.
Web search and the Bonzagni 1512 and Caprile 1519 Este-Hungary siblings for a printed decipherment or shared key: Bonzagni is a different alphabet, Caprile's 1519 key is itself not built.

outcome.notes: Attempted, open. Needs a consistent second transcription of both cipher pages of R1126 (about 1,800 columns) and a decision on the cipher unit before a ciphertext-only attack is meaningful; no key or decipherment known.
